title: On-call notes & runbook draft: pager noise, missing metrics, SLO-burn handling
content:
Summary
------
Quick working notes from several recent on-call rotations where we saw high pager bounce (multiple flapping alerts), a correlated SLO burn alert, and in at least one case the primary service metric (request_latency_seconds) stopped reporting resulting in an auto-escalation. This is a living draft runbook + tuning backlog for reducing noise and improving resilience to missing metrics.

Context / why this matters
- Two pagers escalate per week on average for latency-based SLOs; ~40% are noisy/repeat within 15m.
- Missing exporter metrics caused a false SLO burn alarm on 2025-01-29 during a deploy window. That generated a P2 incident and unnecessary paging to multiple on-callers.
- Goal: reduce noisy pages by 60% over next quarter and add fallback checks for SLO alerts if metric telemetry is degraded.

Incident highlights (recent examples)
- 2025-01-29 02:12 UTC: SLO burn alert triggered (SLO: p99_latency > 500ms over 10m). Pagerduty escalation fired to oncall-sre@pd. Root cause: request_latency_seconds metric absent for ~7 minutes due to a metrics exporter crash on a subset of pods; Prometheus scrape samples dropped to 0 and the alert rule evaluated as "no data -> fire" (we currently treat no data as firing for burn windows).
- 2025-02-07 16:40 UTC: Repeated high-latency alerts from frontend cluster — resolved after 4 minutes by a rolling restart of a misbehaving cache instance. Many alerts were duplicate (per-zone) and many on-callers got paged because we have no effective dedupe for cross-zone firing.

Primary failure modes observed
1) Missing metrics (exporter crash, scrape config mismatch, retention/TSDB compaction) -> alert rules that don't guard against no-data fire spuriously.
2) Unbounded per-instance alerts (alerts firing for each host/pod) -> high fanout.
3) Flapping alerts from marginal thresholds where request distribution shifts briefly (cache warmups, GC pauses).
4) Lack of contextual enrichment: pages do not include : the % of missing targets, last good sample time, last deploy id, and runbook quick links.

Immediate mitigation patterns (to be used during on-call)
- Quick triage checklist when SLO burn fires and metric is missing:
  1. Check metric health: Grafana panel for request_latency_seconds - look for "targets" and last samples.
  2. Confirm Prometheus target count (prometheus/instance_targets endpoint) and scrape status.
  3. If exporter down on small subset: run kubectl -n <ns> get pods -l app=exporter && kubectl logs -f <pod> to identify crashloop.
  4. If large-scale missing metrics: mark alert as "potential telemetry gap" and silence SLO alert for 10m while investigating (use PagerDuty/Alertmanager silence, annotate incident).
  5. Fallback: run synthetic canary query against ingress (curl synthetic endpoint /health/latency) and use that as temporary telemetry for SLO evaluation.
  6. Communicate: post short status in #sre-oncall channel and update incident ticket.

Draft runbook steps (step-by-step)
- When a latency SLO alert fires:
  Step 0: Do not immediately escalate to team leads until step 3 is done unless there's clear downstream customer impact reported.
  Step 1: Open Grafana (SLO dashboard) link in the alert. Check: p99, p95, request rate, and active target count.
  Step 2: Check Prometheus targets page and Prometheus alert evaluation logs (promtool/alertmanager). Command snippets: curl -s http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/targets | jq '.data.activeTargets | length'
  Step 3: If metric health shows "no data" or fewer targets than expected (>20% missing), treat as telemetry gap:
    - Create temporary Alertmanager silence for the SLO alert for 10m with annotation "telemetry-check"
    - Run: kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=metric-exporter -o wide; restart nodes/pods causing gap if obvious.
  Step 4: If metrics present and latency actually high, follow the latency troubleshooting checklist: check deploys in last 30m, backend error rates, cache hit ratio, and recent infra alarms (CPU, network).
  Step 5: If paging multiple on-callers due to per-pod alerts, switch to grouping in Alertmanager (group_by: [service, region]) and reduce per-pod alert severity to advisory.

Alert rule changes proposed (high-level)
- Change "no data" evaluation semantics for SLO burn rules: require at least 70% of expected targets to report metrics; if below, suppress SLO->page and instead generate a telemetry-health ticket.
- Add a short "grace window" (2m) for p99 spikes for autoscaling/cold-start windows before count as SLO burn.
- Group pod-level latency alerts into single service-level alert using label_grouping (region, service) to prevent fanout.
- Add rate-limited paging: rely on a single primary page with escalation rather than multi-target bursts.

Metrics backlog (what to add or improve)
- Add exporter_up_count: count of up exporters per service (for quick health panels).
- Instrumented heartbeat metric from each deployment that Prometheus treats as required.
- Add gauge: scrape_lag_seconds per target to detect slow scraping.
- Synthetic latency metric emitted by canary service (slo_canary_latency_seconds) to act as fallback if real metrics missing.

Alert enrichment & content improvements
- Page should include: last_sample_time, targets_reporting_pct, link to last deploy (CI job id), relevant runbook link, recent incident id if any.
- Use template variables in Alertmanager/Grafana to populate these fields automatically.

Tuning experiments (A/B testing alerts)
- Experiment A (2 weeks): change SLO alert no-data handling to "require 70% targets" and measure weekly pager count; compare to baseline. Owner: Daniel Park.
- Experiment B (4 weeks): enable grouping and rate-limited escalation for per-pod alerts. Owner: Leah Martinez.
- Track: weekly pager counts, mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), and false-positive rate estimated by postmortem classification.

Longer-term items / platform changes
- Centralized telemetry health service that aggregates exporter liveness and calculates "targets_reporting_pct" for each SLO.
- Integrate synthetic canaries into SLO evaluation pipeline as a fallback data source when primary telemetry is degraded.
- Improve Prometheus federation / HA to reduce single-point scrape gaps.
- Add a lightweight ML-based deduper that collapses symptomatically identical alerts (same stacktrace, same deploy, same region).

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- How should SLO policies define "no data" semantics consistently across product teams? Need product/infra alignment.
- Should we convert some SLOs to "observability SLOs" (health of telemetry) vs product SLOs?
- Is Alertmanager good place to implement the 70% target gating, or do we need a pre-eval step?

Action items (owners & ETA)
- Add exporter_up_count metric and basic Grafana panel — Omar Farouk — 2025-03-12.
- Implement 70% target gating as a safety check in the SLO evaluation pipeline — Daniel Park — prototype by 2025-03-21.
- Create alert templates with enriched fields including last_sample_time and targets_reporting_pct — Leah Martinez — 2025-03-05 (in progress).
- Run two-week A/B experiment on no-data gating — Daniel Park — start 2025-03-10.

Notes from on-call (freeform):
- "If you see SLO fire at 03:xx, first check prometheus target counts. Too often we page for a single hotspot in a k8s node and it's due to kube-proxy flakiness." — Omar
- "We should avoid immediate broad escalation for SLOs unless there's confirmed customer impact. A short human check is cheap compared to waking entire team." — Leah

Meeting cadence
- Weekly sync (SRE Alerting) to review pager metrics and tune experiments — Wednesdays 09:30.
- Postmortem quick review within 48h for any page that led to >15 min effort or more than 2 on-callers involved.

Appendix: quick commands
- Check prometheus targets: curl -s http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/targets | jq '.data.activeTargets | length'
- List exporter pods: kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=metric-exporter -o wide
- Restart exporter: kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/metric-exporter
- Silence in Alertmanager: curl -XPOST -d '{"matchers":[{"name":"alertname","value":"SLOBurn"}],"startsAt":"now","endsAt":"+10m","createdBy":"oncall","comment":"telemetry gap"}' http://alertmanager/api/v2/silences

End.

(Work-in-progress; share feedback in #sre-oncall or add comments inline on this doc.)
